## {.title-slide}

::: {.main-title}
Distance, Mobility, and Mode Choice
:::

::: {.subtitle}
A Spatial Analysis of School Travel Behaviour in Ireland
:::

::: {.authors}
**Judith Beltrán López**  
**Sananthaa Jagadesan Senthamaraikannan**
:::

## {.no-title}

![](images/rte_notice.png){width="80%" fig-align="center"}


## Background

School travel is not only a question of **individual choice** — it is also shaped by **distance, school location, and educational provision**.

- Walking and cycling to school can improve health, learning, traffic congestion, and emissions.
- In Ireland, low active travel is often explained as a need for “behaviour change”.
- However, active travel does **not simply follow population density**.
- Instead, it is linked to the spatial distribution of schools and inequalities in access.


## Objectives

Working with **official statistics**, which usually provide **aggregated data**, creates challenges for analysing school travel behaviour at a detailed spatial level.

::: {.incremental}
1. Map and analyse the spatial distribution of schools across Ireland.

2. Examine the distance between students’ residential locations and their schools, and investigate student mobility related to school attendance.

3. Analyse school travel behaviour and assess the prevalence of healthy versus less healthy commuting modes.

4. Explore the relationship between school proximity, travel mode, and potential health implications.
:::

## Datasets: School Data

The school dataset comes from the **Irish Department of Education** and provides information for individual schools.

::: {.incremental}
- Includes data for **primary** and **post-primary** schools.
- Contains information on **enrolment figures** by school.
- Primary school data also includes **class size information**.
- Post-primary data includes specific categories such as **fee-paying** and **boarding schools**.
- This dataset helps describe the **spatial distribution and size of schools** across Ireland.
:::

## Datasets: School Data {.map-slide}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyr)
library(leaflet)
schools_df <- readr::read_csv("data/School_Data_Eircode_2024_2025.csv",
  locale = readr::locale(encoding = "Latin1"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

schools_sf <- schools_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(school_latitude), !is.na(school_longitude)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("school_longitude", "school_latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

enrol <- schools_sf$total_2024_2025
enrol[is.na(enrol)] <- 0
radius <- scales::rescale(enrol, to = c(2, 9))

ireland_counties <- st_read("data/gadm41_IRL_shp/gadm41_IRL_2.shp", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

county_counts <- schools_df %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(!is.na(county)) %>%
  count(county, name = "n_schools")

ireland_counties <- ireland_counties %>%
  left_join(county_counts, by = c("NAME_1" = "county")) %>%
  mutate(n_schools = replace_na(n_schools, 0),
                hover_label = paste0(NAME_1, ": ", n_schools, " schools"))

leaflet(
  options = leafletOptions(zoomControl = TRUE, scrollWheelZoom = TRUE)
) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) %>%

  addPolygons(
    data = ireland_counties,
    fillOpacity = 0,
    color = "black",
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 0.8,
    label = ~hover_label,
    labelOptions = labelOptions(
      direction = "auto",
      textsize = "14px",
      style = list("font-weight" = "bold", "padding" = "6px 8px")
    ),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 3,
      color = "black",
      bringToFront = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%

  addCircleMarkers(
    data = schools_sf,
    lng = ~school_longitude,
    lat = ~school_latitude,
    radius = radius,
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.65,
    color = "#a80050",
    popup = NULL
  ) %>%

  fitBounds(
    lng1 = min(schools_sf$school_longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    lat1 = min(schools_sf$school_latitude,  na.rm = TRUE),
    lng2 = max(schools_sf$school_longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    lat2 = max(schools_sf$school_latitude,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```


## Datasets: Census Data

The census dataset comes from the **Central Statistics Office (CSO)** and provides demographic and socio-economic information at small-area level.

::: {.incremental}
- Includes population characteristics such as **age, sex, households, and families**.
- Provides socio-economic variables related to **education, social class, occupation, and commuting**.
- Contains information on **housing, car availability, and internet access**.
- Small-area data helps capture local demographic conditions around schools.
- These variables are used to explain how local context may influence school travel behaviour.
:::

## Datasets: Census

```{r active-transport-urban-rural}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "100%"

urb_rural_df <- read_csv("data/SAPS_2022_Small_Area_UR_171024.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    category = str_extract(UR_Category_Desc, "(?<=\\.).*")
  ) %>%
  select(
    "GEOGID", "category",
    "T11_1_FSCCC", "T11_1_BISCCC",
    "T11_1_TSCCC", "T11_1_NSSCCC", "T11_1_WMFHSCCC"
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(
    urban_rural = case_when(
      category %in% c(
        " Cities",
        " Satellite Urban Towns",
        " Independent urban towns"
      ) ~ "Urban",
      
      category %in% c(
        " Rural areas with high urban influence",
        " Rural areas with moderate urban influence",
        " Highly rural/remote areas"
      ) ~ "Rural",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(geogid = GEOGID) %>%
  mutate(
    denom = T11_1_TSCCC - T11_1_WMFHSCCC - T11_1_NSSCCC,
    perc_active = ifelse(
      denom > 0,
      100 * (T11_1_FSCCC + T11_1_BISCCC) / denom,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

plot_df <- urb_rural_df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(perc_active),
    perc_active >= 0,
    perc_active <= 100,
    !is.na(urban_rural)
  )

p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = perc_active)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    binwidth = 5,
    boundary = 0,
    closed = "left",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_density(
    aes(color = category),
    trim = TRUE,
    linewidth = 1,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ urban_rural, nrow = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Percentage using active transport",
    y = "Density",
    title = "Active Transport Distribution by Urban/Rural"
  ) +
  guides(color = "none") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 16),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

ggplotly(p) %>%
  layout(
    height = 520,
    showlegend = FALSE,
    margin = list(l = 70, r = 30, t = 70, b = 70)
  )
```

## Kriging

Kriging is a **spatial interpolation method** used to predict values at locations where we do not have observations.

::: {.incremental}
- It uses observed spatial data to estimate values at unsampled locations.
- Predictions are based on **nearby observations** and their spatial correlation.
- The spatial structure is described using a **variogram**.
- Points closer to the prediction location usually receive more weight.
- Kriging also provides a measure of **prediction uncertainty**.
:::

## Model

::: {.model-flow}
**Proportion of students using a travel mode**  
↓  
**Beta distribution**  
↓  
**Explained by distance, travel time, accessibility,  
and school context**
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Designed for continuous proportions between **0 and 1**.
- Uses a **logit link** to keep predicted values inside the valid range.
- Estimates both the relationship between variables and the uncertainty around those relationships.
:::

## Model: Implementation

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

model_urban_krig <- brm(
  formula = perc_active_beta ~ ilr_pct_0_12 + ilr_pct_13_21 + ilr_pct_22_40 + 
    ilr_pct_41_70 + ilr_pct_71plus + ilr_pct_0car + ilr_pct_1car + 
    ilr_pct_2plus + ilr_pct_none_primary + ilr_pct_secondary + 
    ilr_pct_tertiary + krig_value + log_places_density,
  data = df_urban_model,
  family = Beta(link = "logit"),
  prior = priors,
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 123,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95)
)
```

::: {.incremental}
::: {.small-text}
- The formula is built dynamically using the selected predictors.
- Weakly informative priors regularise the model estimates.
- The model is fitted separately for the **urban dataset**.
- Four chains and 4000 iterations improve posterior estimation.
- `adapt_delta = 0.95` helps reduce sampling problems.
:::
:::

## Model: Urban Results

```{r krig-marginal-interactive}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "100%"

df_urban_model <- readRDS("model/data2/df_urban_model.rds")
model_urban_krig <- readRDS("model/models/model_urban_krig.rds")
formula_beta <- readRDS("model/models/formula_beta.rds")
urb_rural_df <- readRDS("model/data2/urb_rural_df.rds")

model_predictors <- all.vars(formula_beta)[-1]

krig_mean <- mean(df_urban_model$krig_value, na.rm = TRUE)
krig_sd <- sd(df_urban_model$krig_value, na.rm = TRUE)

krig_grid <- seq(
  min(df_urban_model$krig_value_z, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(df_urban_model$krig_value_z, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 100
)

newdata_krig <- as_tibble(
  matrix(0, nrow = length(krig_grid), ncol = length(model_predictors))
)

names(newdata_krig) <- model_predictors

newdata_krig <- newdata_krig %>%
  mutate(
    krig_value_z = krig_grid,
    krig_value_original = krig_value_z * krig_sd + krig_mean
  )

pred_krig <- fitted(
  model_urban_krig,
  newdata = newdata_krig,
  scale = "response",
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975)
)

plot_krig <- bind_cols(
  newdata_krig,
  as_tibble(pred_krig)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Estimate_pct = Estimate * 100,
    Q2.5_pct = Q2.5 * 100,
    Q97.5_pct = Q97.5 * 100
  )

p <- ggplot(
  plot_krig,
  aes(x = krig_value_original, y = Estimate_pct)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = Q2.5_pct, ymax = Q97.5_pct),
    alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Marginal Prediction for Kriging Value",
    subtitle = "Other predictors fixed at their average standardized value",
    x = "Kriging value (density of school places per 100 students)",
    y = "Predicted active percentage"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplotly(p) %>%
  layout(
    height = 520,
    margin = list(l = 70, r = 40, t = 80, b = 70)
  )
```

## Travel Time

```{r travel-time-routes}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

options(java.parameters = "-Xmx8G")
library(r5r)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(dplyr)

r5r_core <- r5r::build_network(data_path = "DATA")

schools_sf <- readRDS("DATA/schools_sf.rds") %>%
  st_transform(4326)

destinations <- schools_sf %>%
  mutate(
    id  = as.character(roll_number),
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[,1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[,2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(id, lon, lat, places) %>%
  filter(lon > -9.15, lon < -8.90, lat > 53.20, lat < 53.35)

origin <- data.frame(id = "origin", lon = -9.0489, lat = 53.2743)

routes <- r5r::detailed_itineraries(
  r5r_network   = r5r_core,
  origins       = origin,
  destinations  = destinations,
  mode          = "WALK",
  max_walk_time = 30,
  verbose       = FALSE
)

r5r::stop_r5(r5r_core)

routes_sf <- routes %>% st_as_sf() %>% filter(mode == "WALK")

pal <- colorNumeric(
  palette = c("#2ca25f", "#fed976", "#fd8d3c"),
  domain  = routes_sf$total_duration
)

leaflet() %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) %>%
  addPolylines(
    data    = routes_sf,
    color   = ~pal(total_duration),
    weight  = 3,
    opacity = 0.9,
    label   = ~paste0(round(total_duration, 1), " min walk"),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 5, opacity = 1, bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    data        = schools_sf %>% filter(as.character(roll_number) %in% destinations$id),
    radius      = 6,
    color       = "#9f1f55",
    fillColor   = "#9f1f55",
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    stroke      = FALSE,
    popup       = ~paste0("<b>", name, "</b><br>Places: ", places)
  ) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = -9.0489, lat = 53.2743,
    radius = 10, color = "black",
    fillColor = "yellow", fillOpacity = 1,
    popup = "Origin — CSA centroid"
  ) %>%
  addLegend(
    pal = pal, values = routes_sf$total_duration,
    title = "Walking time (min)", position = "bottomright"
  ) %>%
  setView(lng = -9.0489, lat = 53.2743, zoom = 14)
```

## Travel time - Walking and Cycling Accessibility Urban CSA

```{r travel-time-boxplots}
## Travel time - Walking and Cycling Accessibility Urban CSA
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "100%"

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(readr)
library(stringr)

access_walk  <- readRDS("DATA/access_walk_clean.rds")
access_cycle <- readRDS("DATA/access_cycle_clean.rds")

urb_rural <- read_csv("data/SAPS_2022_Small_Area_UR_171024.csv") %>%
  mutate(
    category    = str_extract(UR_Category_Desc, "(?<=\\.).*"),
    urban_rural = case_when(
      category %in% c(" Cities", " Satellite Urban Towns", " Independent urban towns") ~ "Urban",
      TRUE ~ "Rural"
    ),
    SA_PUB2022 = as.character(GEOGID)
  ) %>%
  select(SA_PUB2022, urban_rural) %>%
  distinct()

urban_csas <- urb_rural %>% filter(urban_rural == "Urban") %>% pull(SA_PUB2022)

access_walk_urban <- access_walk %>%
  mutate(SA_PUB2022 = as.character(id)) %>%
  filter(SA_PUB2022 %in% urban_csas) %>%
  mutate(accessibility_log = log10(accessibility + 1))

access_cycle_urban <- access_cycle %>%
  mutate(SA_PUB2022 = as.character(id)) %>%
  filter(SA_PUB2022 %in% urban_csas) %>%
  mutate(accessibility_log = log10(accessibility + 1))

p_walk <- access_walk_urban %>%
  filter(accessibility > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(cutoff), y = accessibility_log)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "red") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
    labels = c("10", "100", "1,000", "10,000")
  ) +
  labs(title = "Walking accessibility",
       x = "Cutoff (minutes)", y = "School places reachable") +
  theme_minimal()

p_cycle <- access_cycle_urban %>%
  filter(accessibility > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(cutoff), y = accessibility_log)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "red") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
    labels = c("10", "100", "1,000", "10,000")
  ) +
  labs(title = "Cycling accessibility",
       x = "Cutoff (minutes)", y = "School places reachable") +
  theme_minimal()

p_walk + p_cycle
```

## Kriging Vs Travel Time

```{r krig-vs-travel}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "100%"

library(plotly)
library(dplyr)

final_df_complete <- readRDS("DATA/final_df_complete.rds") %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry()

compare_df <- final_df_complete %>%
  filter(
    urban_rural == "Urban",
    !is.na(perc_active),
    !is.na(krig_value),
    !is.na(access_walk_30),
    krig_value > 0,
    access_walk_30 > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log10_krig    = log10(krig_value     + 1),
    log10_walk_30 = log10(access_walk_30 + 1)
  )

p_krig <- plot_ly(compare_df,
        x = ~log10_krig, y = ~perc_active,
        type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(opacity = 0.3, color = "#e74c3c", size = 3),
        text = ~paste("Kriging (log10):", round(log10_krig, 2),
                      "<br>Active travel:", round(perc_active, 1), "%"),
        hoverinfo = "text") %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Kriging school place density",
      tickvals = c(1, 2, 3),
      ticktext = c("10", "100", "1,000")
    ),
    yaxis = list(title = "% active travel"),
    title = "Kriging"
  )

p_walk <- plot_ly(compare_df,
        x = ~log10_walk_30, y = ~perc_active,
        type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(opacity = 0.3, color = "#2980b9", size = 3),
        text = ~paste("Walk (log10):", round(log10_walk_30, 2),
                      "<br>Active travel:", round(perc_active, 1), "%"),
        hoverinfo = "text") %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = "School places reachable by walking",
      tickvals = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
      ticktext = c("10", "100", "1,000", "10,000")
    ),
    yaxis = list(title = "% active travel"),
    title = "r5r Walking"
  )

subplot(p_krig, p_walk,
        nrows = 1, shareY = TRUE, titleX = TRUE) %>%
  layout(
    title      = "Kriging vs Walking accessibility - Urban CSAs",
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
```


## Model: Urban Results - Travel Time

```{r walk-marginal}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-width: "100%"

library(brms)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

df_urban_model   <- readRDS("DATA/df_urban_model_walk.rds")
model_urban_walk <- readRDS("DATA/model_urban_walk.rds")
formula_beta     <- readRDS("DATA/formula_beta_walk.rds")

model_predictors <- all.vars(formula_beta)[-1]

walk_grid <- seq(
  min(df_urban_model$log10_walk_30, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(df_urban_model$log10_walk_30, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 100
)

newdata_walk <- as_tibble(
  matrix(0, nrow = length(walk_grid), ncol = length(model_predictors))
)
names(newdata_walk) <- model_predictors

newdata_walk <- newdata_walk %>%
  mutate(log10_walk_30 = walk_grid)

pred_walk <- fitted(
  model_urban_walk,
  newdata = newdata_walk,
  scale   = "response",
  probs   = c(0.125, 0.875)
)

plot_walk <- bind_cols(newdata_walk, as_tibble(pred_walk)) %>%
  mutate(
    Estimate_pct = Estimate * 100,
    Q2.5_pct     = Q12.5 * 100,
    Q97.5_pct    = Q87.5 * 100
  )

p <- ggplot(plot_walk, aes(x = log10_walk_30, y = Estimate_pct)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q2.5_pct, ymax = Q97.5_pct), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4),
    labels = c("0", "10", "100", "1,000", "10,000")
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Effect of walking accessibility on active travel",
    subtitle = "Other predictors fixed at their average standardised value",
    x        = "School places reachable by walking (30 min)",
    y        = "Active travel (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

ggplotly(p) %>%
  layout(height = 480, margin = list(l = 70, r = 40, t = 80, b = 70))
```
```

## Model: Improvements

::: {.incremental}
- Include a **spatial structure** in the model to account for geographic dependence between schools or areas.

- Consider **zero-inflated beta models** if the response variable contains many exact zero values.

- Explore the **beta distribution shape parameters**, especially alpha, to better understand the distribution of active travel proportions.

- Consider **zero- and one-inflated beta models** if the response variable contains many exact 0 and 1 values.

:::

## Next Steps

::: {.incremental}
- Estimate the **rural model** and compare its results with the urban model.

- Address the limitation that our **outcome data is restricted**, which may affect model interpretation.

- Run separate analyses by **school type** (primary and secondary), while acknowledging possible data limitations.

- Repeat the workflow using **settlement-level data**, which can provide information for the whole town rather than only individual schools.
:::


## Conclusions

::: {.incremental}
- School travel behaviour is strongly shaped by **spatial accessibility**, not only by individual preferences.

- Combining **school data, census variables, kriging, and travel-time measures** creates a richer final dataset for analysing active travel.

- Urban and rural areas show different accessibility patterns, so they should be modelled separately.

- Bayesian beta regression is appropriate for modelling **active travel proportions**, while also quantifying uncertainty.

- The analysis highlights the limitations of aggregated official statistics for detailed spatial mobility research.
:::
